2900 24th Avenue N, Birmingham | Jefferson, AL | 2026-09-23
Prepared for William James Ernst / Syncranicity LLC. No offer, expenditure or signature is authorized. Seller has not accepted these terms. Local real-estate counsel must resolve consideration, licensing/disclosures, assignment, remedies and recording for this specific transaction.

1. PARTIES AND PROPERTY. [Verified record owner and authorized signatory] (Seller) grants [verified Syncranicity legal entity] (Optionee) an exclusive option on approximately 11.0 gross acres marketed as 2900 24th Avenue N, Birmingham. Published identifiers: 22-00-24-2-014-001.001. Published references only; exact land, owner and title are not verified.. Exhibit A must contain an approved legal description, survey boundary and complete APN schedule. Parent references and proposed splits are not sufficient. Verify tenants, liens, access, mineral/water rights and all sellers before execution.

2. PURCHASE PRICE. Proposed price anchor $750,000, the advertised ask or expressly calculated advertised acreage price, not an agreed price or appraisal. Final agreement must fix land, improvements, acreage adjustments, exclusions, fixtures and broker commissions. Listing price limitations: Advertised total ask; availability, scope and price have not been confirmed by seller.

3. OPTION CONSIDERATION AND TERM. Opening proposal: $500 for 180 days after execution and delivery of agreed title/authority documents. Escrow pays only under counsel-approved release instructions. State when consideration is earned and refundable: proposed refunds for seller breach, defective authority or uncured agreed title conditions, otherwise earned after the agreed objection period. Credit to purchase price at closing. No payment has been authorized. Low proposed consideration may be rejected by Seller; no acceptance probability is assumed.

4. EXTENSION. One additional 180 days for $1,000, with written notice before expiry and the same agreed credit/refund treatment. No automatic extension. Extend only if the project evidence, buyer engagement, funding and policy gates independently pass. A 360-day control window is a negotiation hypothesis, not a promise of power delivery. The intended monetizable milestone is an assignable, studyable and buyer-accepted development path; energization may take longer. If required evidence plus closing buffer cannot fit, negotiate longer affordable control or stop.

5. DOCUMENTS, INQUIRIES AND ACCESS. Within ten business days Seller provides existing title, surveys, easements, leases, environmental reports, utility correspondence and planning/fiber records. Seller authorizes nonbinding feasibility inquiries for a 20–30 MW facility-load hypothesis. Noninvasive access requires reasonable notice and agreed insurance. Invasive work requires separate written consent, scoped insurance and restoration obligations. Do not indemnify pre-existing conditions merely discovered. No construction, service reservation, lien, borrowing or obligation may bind Seller without separate written consent.

6. PARCEL CONDITIONS. Specific issues: Month-to-month occupant and prior industrial use; confirm vacant delivery, Phase I and utility load path.
First proof: Ask the broker for active status, current price, complete APNs/survey and existing utility/environmental documents. Resolve this first: Month-to-month occupant and prior industrial use; confirm vacant delivery, Phase I and utility load path.
Before exercise require satisfactory title/legal access, net usable layout, permissible DC/generator use, environmental/civil conditions, water/cooling/fire arrangements, a written utility delivery/supply/tariff/upgrade/credit path, diverse carrier routes with capacity/latency/date/cost, and a funded assignee or sponsor. Neither ordinary electrical service nor neighboring data centers establish available capacity. A 20–30 MW IT-load requirement must be rescreened with the buyer's cooling and PUE assumptions.

7. ASSIGNMENT AND RELIANCE. Proposed express right to assign the entire option to an affiliate or qualified funded developer on written notice and required disclosures, including sharing diligence under confidentiality. Specify seller consent, assignment compensation disclosures, change of control, any public/park covenants, original Optionee release and assignee assumption. No utility capacity or consultant reliance rights transfer unless separately permitted in writing. Seek transferable report reliance and application rights. No brokerage exemption, marketing authority or entitlement to compensation is assumed.

8. EXERCISE AND CLOSING. Exercise only by timely written notice under the final agreement. Proposed closing within 30 days, with a stated outside date and title objection/cure process. Complete escrow agent, deed, title standard, liens, taxes/prorations, closing costs, commissions, vacant possession and tenant rights. Optionee has no unconditional purchase obligation before valid exercise. A funded developer, not assumed founder financing, must cover the purchase balance and project obligations.

9. EXCLUSIVITY AND PROTECTION. During an enforceable paid option Seller cannot convey or encumber the property inconsistently with the granted rights. Resolve existing listing agreements and brokers. Specify confidentiality exceptions for authorized utilities, authorities, advisors and potential assignees. Any memorandum, recording, release, noncircumvention or publicity term requires negotiated language and local review.

10. TERMINATION, DEFAULT AND LOCAL TERMS. Complete notice, cure, casualty/condemnation, termination/refund rights, remedies, liability limits, venue, governing law, integration and required disclosures. No specific-performance or recordability assurance is made across states. Signature blocks and unresolved brackets must be completed by counsel after all gates pass.

ILLUSTRATIVE CASH PLAN — NOT QUOTED OR FUNDED
$500 initial + $1,000 possible extension = $1,500 control consideration. A proposed $2,500 maximum initial learning/legal envelope makes $4,000 modeled loss if both fees and the envelope are spent and nothing is recovered. Actual professional fees, studies, application deposits, upgrades and closing costs are unquoted; $4,000 is not an all-in project estimate. Decline or obtain separate funded approval for work beyond the envelope. Respect existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative soft-control caps, one paid position, company reserve and repeat-attempt funding tests. Remaining company cash is unknown. Begin with document requests and a nonbinding no-deposit terms indication; it does not secure exclusivity.
If both fees are credited, nominal land price balance is $748,500 plus costs. The buyer/sponsor must fund it. Assignment premium is UNKNOWN. Illustrative retained receipts of $25,000 less $4,000 costs = $21,000 pretax profit; zero receipts = $4,000 loss. Break-even is 16% under those assumptions, or 24% after the project policy's 1.5 error buffer (above its 20% initial-option floor). These are economic hurdles, not forecasts. They exclude founder time and unquoted costs and must be recalculated from actual terms.

ASSIGNMENT ASSESSMENT: NOT ESTIMABLE. No supported T, D, B or C probability, acceptable seller control or buyer payment commitment has been established. Planning success definition: lawful cash assignment within 12 months after acceptable control and before expiry, producing at least $10,000 pretax net profit after all project costs. The 360-day option expires earlier than a full year, so its expiry controls. This target is not a prediction.

Exhibit A must contain an approved legal description, survey boundary and complete APN schedule. Parent references and proposed splits are not sufficient. Verify tenants, liens, access, mineral/water rights and all sellers before execution.

2. PURCHASE PRICE. Proposed price anchor $1,750,000, the advertised ask or expressly calculated advertised acreage price, not an agreed price or appraisal. Final agreement must fix land, improvements, acreage adjustments, exclusions, fixtures and broker commissions. Listing price limitations: Reviewed current page $1,750,000; other feeds $1,900,000. Reconfirm seller price.

3. OPTION CONSIDERATION AND TERM. Opening proposal: $500 for 180 days after execution and delivery of agreed title/authority documents. Escrow pays only under counsel-approved release instructions. State when consideration is earned and refundable: proposed refunds for seller breach, defective authority or uncured agreed title conditions, otherwise earned after the agreed objection period. Credit to purchase price at closing. No payment has been authorized. Low proposed consideration may be rejected by Seller; no acceptance probability is assumed.

4. EXTENSION. One additional 180 days for $1,000, with written notice before expiry and the same agreed credit/refund treatment. No automatic extension. Extend only if the project evidence, buyer engagement, funding and policy gates independently pass. A 360-day control window is a negotiation hypothesis, not a promise of power delivery. The intended monetizable milestone is an assignable, studyable and buyer-accepted development path; energization may take longer. If required evidence plus closing buffer cannot fit, negotiate longer affordable control or stop.

5. DOCUMENTS, INQUIRIES AND ACCESS. Within ten business days Seller provides existing title, surveys, easements, leases, environmental reports, utility correspondence and planning/fiber records. Seller authorizes nonbinding feasibility inquiries for a 20–30 MW facility-load hypothesis. Noninvasive access requires reasonable notice and agreed insurance. Invasive work requires separate written consent, scoped insurance and restoration obligations. Do not indemnify pre-existing conditions merely discovered. No construction, service reservation, lien, borrowing or obligation may bind Seller without separate written consent.

First proof: Ask the broker for active status, current price, complete APNs/survey and existing utility/environmental documents. Resolve this first: Current page asks $1.75m versus $1.9m on other feeds; confirm price, prior fill/soil operations and net area.

Neither ordinary electrical service nor neighboring data centers establish available capacity. A 20–30 MW IT-load requirement must be rescreened with the buyer's cooling and PUE assumptions.

7. ASSIGNMENT AND RELIANCE. Proposed express right to assign the entire option to an affiliate or qualified funded developer on written notice and required disclosures, including sharing diligence under confidentiality. Specify seller consent, assignment compensation disclosures, change of control, any public/park covenants, original Optionee release and assignee assumption. No utility capacity or consultant reliance rights transfer unless separately permitted in writing. Seek transferable report reliance and application rights. No brokerage exemption, marketing authority or entitlement to compensation is assumed.

8. EXERCISE AND CLOSING. Exercise only by timely written notice under the final agreement. Proposed closing within 30 days, with a stated outside date and title objection/cure process. Complete escrow agent, deed, title standard, liens, taxes/prorations, closing costs, commissions, vacant possession and tenant rights. Optionee has no unconditional purchase obligation before valid exercise. A funded developer, not assumed founder financing, must cover the purchase balance and project obligations.

9. EXCLUSIVITY AND PROTECTION. During an enforceable paid option Seller cannot convey or encumber the property inconsistently with the granted rights. Resolve existing listing agreements and brokers. Specify confidentiality exceptions for authorized utilities, authorities, advisors and potential assignees. Any memorandum, recording, release, noncircumvention or publicity term requires negotiated language and local review.

10. TERMINATION, DEFAULT AND LOCAL TERMS. Complete notice, cure, casualty/condemnation, termination/refund rights, remedies, liability limits, venue, governing law, integration and required disclosures. No specific-performance or recordability assurance is made across states. Signature blocks and unresolved brackets must be completed by counsel after all gates pass.

$500 initial + $1,000 possible extension = $1,500 control consideration. A proposed $2,500 maximum initial learning/legal envelope makes $4,000 modeled loss if both fees and the envelope are spent and nothing is recovered. Actual professional fees, studies, application deposits, upgrades and closing costs are unquoted; $4,000 is not an all-in project estimate. Decline or obtain separate funded approval for work beyond the envelope. Respect existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative soft-control caps, one paid position, company reserve and repeat-attempt funding tests. Remaining company cash is unknown. Begin with document requests and a nonbinding no-deposit terms indication; it does not secure exclusivity.

Illustrative retained receipts of $25,000 less $4,000 costs = $21,000 pretax profit; zero receipts = $4,000 loss. Break-even is 16% under those assumptions, or 24% after the project policy's 1.5 error buffer (above its 20% initial-option floor). These are economic hurdles, not forecasts. They exclude founder time and unquoted costs and must be recalculated from actual terms.

ASSIGNMENT ASSESSMENT: NOT ESTIMABLE. No supported T, D, B or C probability, acceptable seller control or buyer payment commitment has been established. Planning success definition: lawful cash assignment within 12 months after acceptable control and before expiry, producing at least $10,000 pretax net profit after all project costs. The 360-day option expires earlier than a full year, so its expiry controls. This target is not a prediction.

ILLUSTRATIVE ASSIGNABLE PURCHASE OPTION — COUNSEL WORKING DRAFT
1908 East Euclid Avenue, Des Moines | Polk, IA | 2026-09-23
Prepared for William James Ernst / Syncranicity LLC. No offer, expenditure or signature is authorized. Seller has not accepted these terms. Local real-estate counsel must resolve consideration, licensing/disclosures, assignment, remedies and recording for this specific transaction.

1. PARTIES AND PROPERTY. [Verified record owner and authorized signatory] (Seller) grants [verified Syncranicity legal entity] (Optionee) an exclusive option on approximately 6.5 gross acres marketed as 1908 East Euclid Avenue, Des Moines. Published identifiers: Not published in retrieved listing. Published references only; exact land, owner and title are not verified.. Exhibit A must contain an approved legal description, survey boundary and complete APN schedule. Parent references and proposed splits are not sufficient. Verify tenants, liens, access, mineral/water rights and all sellers before execution.

2. PURCHASE PRICE. Proposed price anchor $850,000, the advertised ask or expressly calculated advertised acreage price, not an agreed price or appraisal. Final agreement must fix land, improvements, acreage adjustments, exclusions, fixtures and broker commissions. Listing price limitations: Advertised total ask; availability, scope and price have not been confirmed by seller.

3. OPTION CONSIDERATION AND TERM. Opening proposal: $500 for 180 days after execution and delivery of agreed title/authority documents. Escrow pays only under counsel-approved release instructions. State when consideration is earned and refundable: proposed refunds for seller breach, defective authority or uncured agreed title conditions, otherwise earned after the agreed objection period. Credit to purchase price at closing. No payment has been authorized. Low proposed consideration may be rejected by Seller; no acceptance probability is assumed.

4. EXTENSION. One additional 180 days for $1,000, with written notice before expiry and the same agreed credit/refund treatment. No automatic extension. Extend only if the project evidence, buyer engagement, funding and policy gates independently pass. A 360-day control window is a negotiation hypothesis, not a promise of power delivery. The intended monetizable milestone is an assignable, studyable and buyer-accepted development path; energization may take longer. If required evidence plus closing buffer cannot fit, negotiate longer affordable control or stop.

5. DOCUMENTS, INQUIRIES AND ACCESS. Within ten business days Seller provides existing title, surveys, easements, leases, environmental reports, utility correspondence and planning/fiber records. Seller authorizes nonbinding feasibility inquiries for a 20–30 MW facility-load hypothesis. Noninvasive access requires reasonable notice and agreed insurance. Invasive work requires separate written consent, scoped insurance and restoration obligations. Do not indemnify pre-existing conditions merely discovered. No construction, service reservation, lien, borrowing or obligation may bind Seller without separate written consent.

6. PARCEL CONDITIONS. Specific issues: Old portal entry; verify active sale, exact zoning, parcel assembly and seller willingness to allow assignment.
First proof: Ask the broker for active status, current price, complete APNs/survey and existing utility/environmental documents. Resolve this first: Old portal entry; verify active sale, exact zoning, parcel assembly and seller willingness to allow assignment.
Before exercise require satisfactory title/legal access, net usable layout, permissible DC/generator use, environmental/civil conditions, water/cooling/fire arrangements, a written utility delivery/supply/tariff/upgrade/credit path, diverse carrier routes with capacity/latency/date/cost, and a funded assignee or sponsor. Neither ordinary electrical service nor neighboring data centers establish available capacity. A 20–30 MW IT-load requirement must be rescreened with the buyer's cooling and PUE assumptions.

7. ASSIGNMENT AND RELIANCE. Proposed express right to assign the entire option to an affiliate or qualified funded developer on written notice and required disclosures, including sharing diligence under confidentiality. Specify seller consent, assignment compensation disclosures, change of control, any public/park covenants, original Optionee release and assignee assumption. No utility capacity or consultant reliance rights transfer unless separately permitted in writing. Seek transferable report reliance and application rights. No brokerage exemption, marketing authority or entitlement to compensation is assumed.

8. EXERCISE AND CLOSING. Exercise only by timely written notice under the final agreement. Proposed closing within 30 days, with a stated outside date and title objection/cure process. Complete escrow agent, deed, title standard, liens, taxes/prorations, closing costs, commissions, vacant possession and tenant rights. Optionee has no unconditional purchase obligation before valid exercise. A funded developer, not assumed founder financing, must cover the purchase balance and project obligations.

9. EXCLUSIVITY AND PROTECTION. During an enforceable paid option Seller cannot convey or encumber the property inconsistently with the granted rights. Resolve existing listing agreements and brokers. Specify confidentiality exceptions for authorized utilities, authorities, advisors and potential assignees. Any memorandum, recording, release, noncircumvention or publicity term requires negotiated language and local review.

10. TERMINATION, DEFAULT AND LOCAL TERMS. Complete notice, cure, casualty/condemnation, termination/refund rights, remedies, liability limits, venue, governing law, integration and required disclosures. No specific-performance or recordability assurance is made across states. Signature blocks and unresolved brackets must be completed by counsel after all gates pass.

ILLUSTRATIVE CASH PLAN — NOT QUOTED OR FUNDED
$500 initial + $1,000 possible extension = $1,500 control consideration. A proposed $2,500 maximum initial learning/legal envelope makes $4,000 modeled loss if both fees and the envelope are spent and nothing is recovered. Actual professional fees, studies, application deposits, upgrades and closing costs are unquoted; $4,000 is not an all-in project estimate. Decline or obtain separate funded approval for work beyond the envelope. Respect existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative soft-control caps, one paid position, company reserve and repeat-attempt funding tests. Remaining company cash is unknown. Begin with document requests and a nonbinding no-deposit terms indication; it does not secure exclusivity.
If both fees are credited, nominal land price balance is $848,500 plus costs. The buyer/sponsor must fund it. Assignment premium is UNKNOWN. Illustrative retained receipts of $25,000 less $4,000 costs = $21,000 pretax profit; zero receipts = $4,000 loss. Break-even is 16% under those assumptions, or 24% after the project policy's 1.5 error buffer (above its 20% initial-option floor). These are economic hurdles, not forecasts. They exclude founder time and unquoted costs and must be recalculated from actual terms.

ASSIGNMENT ASSESSMENT: NOT ESTIMABLE. No supported T, D, B or C probability, acceptable seller control or buyer payment commitment has been established. Planning success definition: lawful cash assignment within 12 months after acceptable control and before expiry, producing at least $10,000 pretax net profit after all project costs. The 360-day option expires earlier than a full year, so its expiry controls. This target is not a prediction.

ILLUSTRATIVE ASSIGNABLE PURCHASE OPTION — COUNSEL WORKING DRAFT
Commander Drive, Arlington | Shelby, TN | 2026-09-23
Prepared for William James Ernst / Syncranicity LLC. No offer, expenditure or signature is authorized. Seller has not accepted these terms. Local real-estate counsel must resolve consideration, licensing/disclosures, assignment, remedies and recording for this specific transaction.

1. PARTIES AND PROPERTY. [Verified record owner and authorized signatory] (Seller) grants [verified Syncranicity legal entity] (Optionee) an exclusive option on approximately 8.66 gross acres marketed as Commander Drive, Arlington. Published identifiers: Not published in retrieved listing. Published references only; exact land, owner and title are not verified.. Exhibit A must contain an approved legal description, survey boundary and complete APN schedule. Parent references and proposed splits are not sufficient. Verify tenants, liens, access, mineral/water rights and all sellers before execution.

2. PURCHASE PRICE. Proposed price anchor $825,000, the advertised ask or expressly calculated advertised acreage price, not an agreed price or appraisal. Final agreement must fix land, improvements, acreage adjustments, exclusions, fixtures and broker commissions. Listing price limitations: Advertised total ask; availability, scope and price have not been confirmed by seller.

3. OPTION CONSIDERATION AND TERM. Opening proposal: $500 for 180 days after execution and delivery of agreed title/authority documents. Escrow pays only under counsel-approved release instructions. State when consideration is earned and refundable: proposed refunds for seller breach, defective authority or uncured agreed title conditions, otherwise earned after the agreed objection period. Credit to purchase price at closing. No payment has been authorized. Low proposed consideration may be rejected by Seller; no acceptance probability is assumed.

4. EXTENSION. One additional 180 days for $1,000, with written notice before expiry and the same agreed credit/refund treatment. No automatic extension. Extend only if the project evidence, buyer engagement, funding and policy gates independently pass. A 360-day control window is a negotiation hypothesis, not a promise of power delivery. The intended monetizable milestone is an assignable, studyable and buyer-accepted development path; energization may take longer. If required evidence plus closing buffer cannot fit, negotiate longer affordable control or stop.

5. DOCUMENTS, INQUIRIES AND ACCESS. Within ten business days Seller provides existing title, surveys, easements, leases, environmental reports, utility correspondence and planning/fiber records. Seller authorizes nonbinding feasibility inquiries for a 20–30 MW facility-load hypothesis. Noninvasive access requires reasonable notice and agreed insurance. Invasive work requires separate written consent, scoped insurance and restoration obligations. Do not indemnify pre-existing conditions merely discovered. No construction, service reservation, lien, borrowing or obligation may bind Seller without separate written consent.

6. PARCEL CONDITIONS. Specific issues: Obtain park covenants, service maps, exact APN and confirmation assignment is permitted.
First proof: Ask the broker for active status, current price, complete APNs/survey and existing utility/environmental documents. Resolve this first: Obtain park covenants, service maps, exact APN and confirmation assignment is permitted.
Before exercise require satisfactory title/legal access, net usable layout, permissible DC/generator use, environmental/civil conditions, water/cooling/fire arrangements, a written utility delivery/supply/tariff/upgrade/credit path, diverse carrier routes with capacity/latency/date/cost, and a funded assignee or sponsor. Neither ordinary electrical service nor neighboring data centers establish available capacity. A 20–30 MW IT-load requirement must be rescreened with the buyer's cooling and PUE assumptions.

7. ASSIGNMENT AND RELIANCE. Proposed express right to assign the entire option to an affiliate or qualified funded developer on written notice and required disclosures, including sharing diligence under confidentiality. Specify seller consent, assignment compensation disclosures, change of control, any public/park covenants, original Optionee release and assignee assumption. No utility capacity or consultant reliance rights transfer unless separately permitted in writing. Seek transferable report reliance and application rights. No brokerage exemption, marketing authority or entitlement to compensation is assumed.

8. EXERCISE AND CLOSING. Exercise only by timely written notice under the final agreement. Proposed closing within 30 days, with a stated outside date and title objection/cure process. Complete escrow agent, deed, title standard, liens, taxes/prorations, closing costs, commissions, vacant possession and tenant rights. Optionee has no unconditional purchase obligation before valid exercise. A funded developer, not assumed founder financing, must cover the purchase balance and project obligations.

9. EXCLUSIVITY AND PROTECTION. During an enforceable paid option Seller cannot convey or encumber the property inconsistently with the granted rights. Resolve existing listing agreements and brokers. Specify confidentiality exceptions for authorized utilities, authorities, advisors and potential assignees. Any memorandum, recording, release, noncircumvention or publicity term requires negotiated language and local review.

10. TERMINATION, DEFAULT AND LOCAL TERMS. Complete notice, cure, casualty/condemnation, termination/refund rights, remedies, liability limits, venue, governing law, integration and required disclosures. No specific-performance or recordability assurance is made across states. Signature blocks and unresolved brackets must be completed by counsel after all gates pass.

ILLUSTRATIVE CASH PLAN — NOT QUOTED OR FUNDED
$500 initial + $1,000 possible extension = $1,500 control consideration. A proposed $2,500 maximum initial learning/legal envelope makes $4,000 modeled loss if both fees and the envelope are spent and nothing is recovered. Actual professional fees, studies, application deposits, upgrades and closing costs are unquoted; $4,000 is not an all-in project estimate. Decline or obtain separate funded approval for work beyond the envelope. Respect existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative soft-control caps, one paid position, company reserve and repeat-attempt funding tests. Remaining company cash is unknown. Begin with document requests and a nonbinding no-deposit terms indication; it does not secure exclusivity.
If both fees are credited, nominal land price balance is $823,500 plus costs. The buyer/sponsor must fund it. Assignment premium is UNKNOWN. Illustrative retained receipts of $25,000 less $4,000 costs = $21,000 pretax profit; zero receipts = $4,000 loss. Break-even is 16% under those assumptions, or 24% after the project policy's 1.5 error buffer (above its 20% initial-option floor). These are economic hurdles, not forecasts. They exclude founder time and unquoted costs and must be recalculated from actual terms.

ASSIGNMENT ASSESSMENT: NOT ESTIMABLE. No supported T, D, B or C probability, acceptable seller control or buyer payment commitment has been established. Planning success definition: lawful cash assignment within 12 months after acceptable control and before expiry, producing at least $10,000 pretax net profit after all project costs. The 360-day option expires earlier than a full year, so its expiry controls. This target is not a prediction.

ILLUSTRATIVE ASSIGNABLE PURCHASE OPTION — COUNSEL WORKING DRAFT
1133 and 1175 E 152nd Street, Cleveland | Cuyahoga, OH | 2026-09-23
Prepared for William James Ernst / Syncranicity LLC. No offer, expenditure or signature is authorized. Seller has not accepted these terms. Local real-estate counsel must resolve consideration, licensing/disclosures, assignment, remedies and recording for this specific transaction.

1. PARTIES AND PROPERTY. [Verified record owner and authorized signatory] (Seller) grants [verified Syncranicity legal entity] (Optionee) an exclusive option on approximately 25.6 gross acres marketed as 1133 and 1175 E 152nd Street, Cleveland. Published identifiers: 115-19-008; 115-20-006 (published, may be partial). Published references only; exact land, owner and title are not verified.. Exhibit A must contain an approved legal description, survey boundary and complete APN schedule. Parent references and proposed splits are not sufficient. Verify tenants, liens, access, mineral/water rights and all sellers before execution.

2. PURCHASE PRICE. Proposed price anchor $1,664,000, the advertised ask or expressly calculated advertised acreage price, not an agreed price or appraisal. Final agreement must fix land, improvements, acreage adjustments, exclusions, fixtures and broker commissions. Listing price limitations: Advertised total ask; availability, scope and price have not been confirmed by seller.

3. OPTION CONSIDERATION AND TERM. Opening proposal: $500 for 180 days after execution and delivery of agreed title/authority documents. Escrow pays only under counsel-approved release instructions. State when consideration is earned and refundable: proposed refunds for seller breach, defective authority or uncured agreed title conditions, otherwise earned after the agreed objection period. Credit to purchase price at closing. No payment has been authorized. Low proposed consideration may be rejected by Seller; no acceptance probability is assumed.

4. EXTENSION. One additional 180 days for $1,000, with written notice before expiry and the same agreed credit/refund treatment. No automatic extension. Extend only if the project evidence, buyer engagement, funding and policy gates independently pass. A 360-day control window is a negotiation hypothesis, not a promise of power delivery. The intended monetizable milestone is an assignable, studyable and buyer-accepted development path; energization may take longer. If required evidence plus closing buffer cannot fit, negotiate longer affordable control or stop.

5. DOCUMENTS, INQUIRIES AND ACCESS. Within ten business days Seller provides existing title, surveys, easements, leases, environmental reports, utility correspondence and planning/fiber records. Seller authorizes nonbinding feasibility inquiries for a 20–30 MW facility-load hypothesis. Noninvasive access requires reasonable notice and agreed insurance. Invasive work requires separate written consent, scoped insurance and restoration obligations. Do not indemnify pre-existing conditions merely discovered. No construction, service reservation, lien, borrowing or obligation may bind Seller without separate written consent.

6. PARCEL CONDITIONS. Specific issues: Former urban industrial land: environmental history, full APN set and net layout need verification.
First proof: Ask the broker for active status, current price, complete APNs/survey and existing utility/environmental documents. Resolve this first: Former urban industrial land: environmental history, full APN set and net layout need verification.
Before exercise require satisfactory title/legal access, net usable layout, permissible DC/generator use, environmental/civil conditions, water/cooling/fire arrangements, a written utility delivery/supply/tariff/upgrade/credit path, diverse carrier routes with capacity/latency/date/cost, and a funded assignee or sponsor. Neither ordinary electrical service nor neighboring data centers establish available capacity. A 20–30 MW IT-load requirement must be rescreened with the buyer's cooling and PUE assumptions.

7. ASSIGNMENT AND RELIANCE. Proposed express right to assign the entire option to an affiliate or qualified funded developer on written notice and required disclosures, including sharing diligence under confidentiality. Specify seller consent, assignment compensation disclosures, change of control, any public/park covenants, original Optionee release and assignee assumption. No utility capacity or consultant reliance rights transfer unless separately permitted in writing. Seek transferable report reliance and application rights. No brokerage exemption, marketing authority or entitlement to compensation is assumed.

8. EXERCISE AND CLOSING. Exercise only by timely written notice under the final agreement. Proposed closing within 30 days, with a stated outside date and title objection/cure process. Complete escrow agent, deed, title standard, liens, taxes/prorations, closing costs, commissions, vacant possession and tenant rights. Optionee has no unconditional purchase obligation before valid exercise. A funded developer, not assumed founder financing, must cover the purchase balance and project obligations.

9. EXCLUSIVITY AND PROTECTION. During an enforceable paid option Seller cannot convey or encumber the property inconsistently with the granted rights. Resolve existing listing agreements and brokers. Specify confidentiality exceptions for authorized utilities, authorities, advisors and potential assignees. Any memorandum, recording, release, noncircumvention or publicity term requires negotiated language and local review.

10. TERMINATION, DEFAULT AND LOCAL TERMS. Complete notice, cure, casualty/condemnation, termination/refund rights, remedies, liability limits, venue, governing law, integration and required disclosures. No specific-performance or recordability assurance is made across states. Signature blocks and unresolved brackets must be completed by counsel after all gates pass.

ILLUSTRATIVE CASH PLAN — NOT QUOTED OR FUNDED
$500 initial + $1,000 possible extension = $1,500 control consideration. A proposed $2,500 maximum initial learning/legal envelope makes $4,000 modeled loss if both fees and the envelope are spent and nothing is recovered. Actual professional fees, studies, application deposits, upgrades and closing costs are unquoted; $4,000 is not an all-in project estimate. Decline or obtain separate funded approval for work beyond the envelope. Respect existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative soft-control caps, one paid position, company reserve and repeat-attempt funding tests. Remaining company cash is unknown. Begin with document requests and a nonbinding no-deposit terms indication; it does not secure exclusivity.
If both fees are credited, nominal land price balance is $1,662,500 plus costs. The buyer/sponsor must fund it. Assignment premium is UNKNOWN. Illustrative retained receipts of $25,000 less $4,000 costs = $21,000 pretax profit; zero receipts = $4,000 loss. Break-even is 16% under those assumptions, or 24% after the project policy's 1.5 error buffer (above its 20% initial-option floor). These are economic hurdles, not forecasts. They exclude founder time and unquoted costs and must be recalculated from actual terms.

ASSIGNMENT ASSESSMENT: NOT ESTIMABLE. No supported T, D, B or C probability, acceptable seller control or buyer payment commitment has been established. Planning success definition: lawful cash assignment within 12 months after acceptable control and before expiry, producing at least $10,000 pretax net profit after all project costs. The 360-day option expires earlier than a full year, so its expiry controls. This target is not a prediction.

ILLUSTRATIVE ASSIGNABLE PURCHASE OPTION — COUNSEL WORKING DRAFT
12 E 151st Street S, Coweta | Wagoner, OK | 2026-09-23
Prepared for William James Ernst / Syncranicity LLC. No offer, expenditure or signature is authorized. Seller has not accepted these terms. Local real-estate counsel must resolve consideration, licensing/disclosures, assignment, remedies and recording for this specific transaction.

1. PARTIES AND PROPERTY. [Verified record owner and authorized signatory] (Seller) grants [verified Syncranicity legal entity] (Optionee) an exclusive option on approximately 12.0 gross acres marketed as 12 E 151st Street S, Coweta. Published identifiers: Not published in retrieved listing. Published references only; exact land, owner and title are not verified.. Exhibit A must contain an approved legal description, survey boundary and complete APN schedule. Parent references and proposed splits are not sufficient. Verify tenants, liens, access, mineral/water rights and all sellers before execution.

2. PURCHASE PRICE. Proposed price anchor $319,900, the advertised ask or expressly calculated advertised acreage price, not an agreed price or appraisal. Final agreement must fix land, improvements, acreage adjustments, exclusions, fixtures and broker commissions. Listing price limitations: Advertised total ask; availability, scope and price have not been confirmed by seller.

3. OPTION CONSIDERATION AND TERM. Opening proposal: $500 for 180 days after execution and delivery of agreed title/authority documents. Escrow pays only under counsel-approved release instructions. State when consideration is earned and refundable: proposed refunds for seller breach, defective authority or uncured agreed title conditions, otherwise earned after the agreed objection period. Credit to purchase price at closing. No payment has been authorized. Low proposed consideration may be rejected by Seller; no acceptance probability is assumed.

4. EXTENSION. One additional 180 days for $1,000, with written notice before expiry and the same agreed credit/refund treatment. No automatic extension. Extend only if the project evidence, buyer engagement, funding and policy gates independently pass. A 360-day control window is a negotiation hypothesis, not a promise of power delivery. The intended monetizable milestone is an assignable, studyable and buyer-accepted development path; energization may take longer. If required evidence plus closing buffer cannot fit, negotiate longer affordable control or stop.

5. DOCUMENTS, INQUIRIES AND ACCESS. Within ten business days Seller provides existing title, surveys, easements, leases, environmental reports, utility correspondence and planning/fiber records. Seller authorizes nonbinding feasibility inquiries for a 20–30 MW facility-load hypothesis. Noninvasive access requires reasonable notice and agreed insurance. Invasive work requires separate written consent, scoped insurance and restoration obligations. Do not indemnify pre-existing conditions merely discovered. No construction, service reservation, lien, borrowing or obligation may bind Seller without separate written consent.

6. PARCEL CONDITIONS. Specific issues: Exact industrial district, APN and utility service absent; cheap price alone is insufficient.
First proof: Ask the broker for active status, current price, complete APNs/survey and existing utility/environmental documents. Resolve this first: Exact industrial district, APN and utility service absent; cheap price alone is insufficient.
Before exercise require satisfactory title/legal access, net usable layout, permissible DC/generator use, environmental/civil conditions, water/cooling/fire arrangements, a written utility delivery/supply/tariff/upgrade/credit path, diverse carrier routes with capacity/latency/date/cost, and a funded assignee or sponsor. Neither ordinary electrical service nor neighboring data centers establish available capacity. A 20–30 MW IT-load requirement must be rescreened with the buyer's cooling and PUE assumptions.

7. ASSIGNMENT AND RELIANCE. Proposed express right to assign the entire option to an affiliate or qualified funded developer on written notice and required disclosures, including sharing diligence under confidentiality. Specify seller consent, assignment compensation disclosures, change of control, any public/park covenants, original Optionee release and assignee assumption. No utility capacity or consultant reliance rights transfer unless separately permitted in writing. Seek transferable report reliance and application rights. No brokerage exemption, marketing authority or entitlement to compensation is assumed.

8. EXERCISE AND CLOSING. Exercise only by timely written notice under the final agreement. Proposed closing within 30 days, with a stated outside date and title objection/cure process. Complete escrow agent, deed, title standard, liens, taxes/prorations, closing costs, commissions, vacant possession and tenant rights. Optionee has no unconditional purchase obligation before valid exercise. A funded developer, not assumed founder financing, must cover the purchase balance and project obligations.

9. EXCLUSIVITY AND PROTECTION. During an enforceable paid option Seller cannot convey or encumber the property inconsistently with the granted rights. Resolve existing listing agreements and brokers. Specify confidentiality exceptions for authorized utilities, authorities, advisors and potential assignees. Any memorandum, recording, release, noncircumvention or publicity term requires negotiated language and local review.

10. TERMINATION, DEFAULT AND LOCAL TERMS. Complete notice, cure, casualty/condemnation, termination/refund rights, remedies, liability limits, venue, governing law, integration and required disclosures. No specific-performance or recordability assurance is made across states. Signature blocks and unresolved brackets must be completed by counsel after all gates pass.

ILLUSTRATIVE CASH PLAN — NOT QUOTED OR FUNDED
$500 initial + $1,000 possible extension = $1,500 control consideration. A proposed $2,500 maximum initial learning/legal envelope makes $4,000 modeled loss if both fees and the envelope are spent and nothing is recovered. Actual professional fees, studies, application deposits, upgrades and closing costs are unquoted; $4,000 is not an all-in project estimate. Decline or obtain separate funded approval for work beyond the envelope. Respect existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative soft-control caps, one paid position, company reserve and repeat-attempt funding tests. Remaining company cash is unknown. Begin with document requests and a nonbinding no-deposit terms indication; it does not secure exclusivity.
If both fees are credited, nominal land price balance is $318,400 plus costs. The buyer/sponsor must fund it. Assignment premium is UNKNOWN. Illustrative retained receipts of $25,000 less $4,000 costs = $21,000 pretax profit; zero receipts = $4,000 loss. Break-even is 16% under those assumptions, or 24% after the project policy's 1.5 error buffer (above its 20% initial-option floor). These are economic hurdles, not forecasts. They exclude founder time and unquoted costs and must be recalculated from actual terms.

ASSIGNMENT ASSESSMENT: NOT ESTIMABLE. No supported T, D, B or C probability, acceptable seller control or buyer payment commitment has been established. Planning success definition: lawful cash assignment within 12 months after acceptable control and before expiry, producing at least $10,000 pretax net profit after all project costs. The 360-day option expires earlier than a full year, so its expiry controls. This target is not a prediction.

ILLUSTRATIVE ASSIGNABLE PURCHASE OPTION — COUNSEL WORKING DRAFT
Enterprise Drive, Allen Park Tech Center — 7.43-acre offer | Wayne, MI | 2026-09-23
Prepared for William James Ernst / Syncranicity LLC. No offer, expenditure or signature is authorized. Seller has not accepted these terms. Local real-estate counsel must resolve consideration, licensing/disclosures, assignment, remedies and recording for this specific transaction.

1. PARTIES AND PROPERTY. [Verified record owner and authorized signatory] (Seller) grants [verified Syncranicity legal entity] (Optionee) an exclusive option on approximately 7.43 gross acres marketed as Enterprise Drive, Allen Park Tech Center — 7.43-acre offer. Published identifiers: 30-008-99-0001-712 (parent reference; offered split unverified). Published references only; exact land, owner and title are not verified.. Exhibit A must contain an approved legal description, survey boundary and complete APN schedule. Parent references and proposed splits are not sufficient. Verify tenants, liens, access, mineral/water rights and all sellers before execution.

2. PURCHASE PRICE. Proposed price anchor $1,114,500, the advertised ask or expressly calculated advertised acreage price, not an agreed price or appraisal. Final agreement must fix land, improvements, acreage adjustments, exclusions, fixtures and broker commissions. Listing price limitations: Calculated: 7.43-acre alternative × $150,000/acre = $1,114,500; split and complete APNs unresolved.

3. OPTION CONSIDERATION AND TERM. Opening proposal: $500 for 180 days after execution and delivery of agreed title/authority documents. Escrow pays only under counsel-approved release instructions. State when consideration is earned and refundable: proposed refunds for seller breach, defective authority or uncured agreed title conditions, otherwise earned after the agreed objection period. Credit to purchase price at closing. No payment has been authorized. Low proposed consideration may be rejected by Seller; no acceptance probability is assumed.

4. EXTENSION. One additional 180 days for $1,000, with written notice before expiry and the same agreed credit/refund treatment. No automatic extension. Extend only if the project evidence, buyer engagement, funding and policy gates independently pass. A 360-day control window is a negotiation hypothesis, not a promise of power delivery. The intended monetizable milestone is an assignable, studyable and buyer-accepted development path; energization may take longer. If required evidence plus closing buffer cannot fit, negotiate longer affordable control or stop.

5. DOCUMENTS, INQUIRIES AND ACCESS. Within ten business days Seller provides existing title, surveys, easements, leases, environmental reports, utility correspondence and planning/fiber records. Seller authorizes nonbinding feasibility inquiries for a 20–30 MW facility-load hypothesis. Noninvasive access requires reasonable notice and agreed insurance. Invasive work requires separate written consent, scoped insurance and restoration obligations. Do not indemnify pre-existing conditions merely discovered. No construction, service reservation, lien, borrowing or obligation may bind Seller without separate written consent.

6. PARCEL CONDITIONS. Specific issues: Price calculated for 7.43-acre alternative; page header emphasizes 17.85; C6C commercial zoning and lot split unresolved.
First proof: Ask the broker for active status, current price, complete APNs/survey and existing utility/environmental documents. Resolve this first: Price calculated for 7.43-acre alternative; page header emphasizes 17.85; C6C commercial zoning and lot split unresolved.
Before exercise require satisfactory title/legal access, net usable layout, permissible DC/generator use, environmental/civil conditions, water/cooling/fire arrangements, a written utility delivery/supply/tariff/upgrade/credit path, diverse carrier routes with capacity/latency/date/cost, and a funded assignee or sponsor. Neither ordinary electrical service nor neighboring data centers establish available capacity. A 20–30 MW IT-load requirement must be rescreened with the buyer's cooling and PUE assumptions.

7. ASSIGNMENT AND RELIANCE. Proposed express right to assign the entire option to an affiliate or qualified funded developer on written notice and required disclosures, including sharing diligence under confidentiality. Specify seller consent, assignment compensation disclosures, change of control, any public/park covenants, original Optionee release and assignee assumption. No utility capacity or consultant reliance rights transfer unless separately permitted in writing. Seek transferable report reliance and application rights. No brokerage exemption, marketing authority or entitlement to compensation is assumed.

8. EXERCISE AND CLOSING. Exercise only by timely written notice under the final agreement. Proposed closing within 30 days, with a stated outside date and title objection/cure process. Complete escrow agent, deed, title standard, liens, taxes/prorations, closing costs, commissions, vacant possession and tenant rights. Optionee has no unconditional purchase obligation before valid exercise. A funded developer, not assumed founder financing, must cover the purchase balance and project obligations.

9. EXCLUSIVITY AND PROTECTION. During an enforceable paid option Seller cannot convey or encumber the property inconsistently with the granted rights. Resolve existing listing agreements and brokers. Specify confidentiality exceptions for authorized utilities, authorities, advisors and potential assignees. Any memorandum, recording, release, noncircumvention or publicity term requires negotiated language and local review.

10. TERMINATION, DEFAULT AND LOCAL TERMS. Complete notice, cure, casualty/condemnation, termination/refund rights, remedies, liability limits, venue, governing law, integration and required disclosures. No specific-performance or recordability assurance is made across states. Signature blocks and unresolved brackets must be completed by counsel after all gates pass.

ILLUSTRATIVE CASH PLAN — NOT QUOTED OR FUNDED
$500 initial + $1,000 possible extension = $1,500 control consideration. A proposed $2,500 maximum initial learning/legal envelope makes $4,000 modeled loss if both fees and the envelope are spent and nothing is recovered. Actual professional fees, studies, application deposits, upgrades and closing costs are unquoted; $4,000 is not an all-in project estimate. Decline or obtain separate funded approval for work beyond the envelope. Respect existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative soft-control caps, one paid position, company reserve and repeat-attempt funding tests. Remaining company cash is unknown. Begin with document requests and a nonbinding no-deposit terms indication; it does not secure exclusivity.
If both fees are credited, nominal land price balance is $1,113,000 plus costs. The buyer/sponsor must fund it. Assignment premium is UNKNOWN. Illustrative retained receipts of $25,000 less $4,000 costs = $21,000 pretax profit; zero receipts = $4,000 loss. Break-even is 16% under those assumptions, or 24% after the project policy's 1.5 error buffer (above its 20% initial-option floor). These are economic hurdles, not forecasts. They exclude founder time and unquoted costs and must be recalculated from actual terms.

ASSIGNMENT ASSESSMENT: NOT ESTIMABLE. No supported T, D, B or C probability, acceptable seller control or buyer payment commitment has been established. Planning success definition: lawful cash assignment within 12 months after acceptable control and before expiry, producing at least $10,000 pretax net profit after all project costs. The 360-day option expires earlier than a full year, so its expiry controls. This target is not a prediction.

[Verified record owner and authorized signatory] (Seller) grants [verified Syncranicity legal entity] (Optionee) an exclusive option on approximately 9.68 gross acres marketed as Eureka Road east of Harrison, Romulus. Published identifiers: Not published in retrieved listing. Published references only; exact land, owner and title are not verified.. Exhibit A must contain an approved legal description, survey boundary and complete APN schedule. Parent references and proposed splits are not sufficient. Verify tenants, liens, access, mineral/water rights and all sellers before execution.

2. PURCHASE PRICE. Proposed price anchor $375,000, the advertised ask or expressly calculated advertised acreage price, not an agreed price or appraisal. Final agreement must fix land, improvements, acreage adjustments, exclusions, fixtures and broker commissions. Listing price limitations: Advertised total ask; availability, scope and price have not been confirmed by seller.

3. OPTION CONSIDERATION AND TERM. Opening proposal: $500 for 180 days after execution and delivery of agreed title/authority documents. Escrow pays only under counsel-approved release instructions. State when consideration is earned and refundable: proposed refunds for seller breach, defective authority or uncured agreed title conditions, otherwise earned after the agreed objection period. Credit to purchase price at closing. No payment has been authorized. Low proposed consideration may be rejected by Seller; no acceptance probability is assumed.

4. EXTENSION. One additional 180 days for $1,000, with written notice before expiry and the same agreed credit/refund treatment. No automatic extension. Extend only if the project evidence, buyer engagement, funding and policy gates independently pass. A 360-day control window is a negotiation hypothesis, not a promise of power delivery. The intended monetizable milestone is an assignable, studyable and buyer-accepted development path; energization may take longer. If required evidence plus closing buffer cannot fit, negotiate longer affordable control or stop.

5. DOCUMENTS, INQUIRIES AND ACCESS. Within ten business days Seller provides existing title, surveys, easements, leases, environmental reports, utility correspondence and planning/fiber records. Seller authorizes nonbinding feasibility inquiries for a 20–30 MW facility-load hypothesis. Noninvasive access requires reasonable notice and agreed insurance. Invasive work requires separate written consent, scoped insurance and restoration obligations. Do not indemnify pre-existing conditions merely discovered. No construction, service reservation, lien, borrowing or obligation may bind Seller without separate written consent.

6. PARCEL CONDITIONS. Specific issues: Approximately 239 by 1,761 feet: narrow geometry may defeat 20–30 MW layout; concept-fit test first, no paid control.
First proof: Ask the broker for active status, current price, complete APNs/survey and existing utility/environmental documents. Resolve this first: Approximately 239 by 1,761 feet: narrow geometry may defeat 20–30 MW layout; concept-fit test first, no paid control.
Before exercise require satisfactory title/legal access, net usable layout, permissible DC/generator use, environmental/civil conditions, water/cooling/fire arrangements, a written utility delivery/supply/tariff/upgrade/credit path, diverse carrier routes with capacity/latency/date/cost, and a funded assignee or sponsor. Neither ordinary electrical service nor neighboring data centers establish available capacity. A 20–30 MW IT-load requirement must be rescreened with the buyer's cooling and PUE assumptions.

7. ASSIGNMENT AND RELIANCE. Proposed express right to assign the entire option to an affiliate or qualified funded developer on written notice and required disclosures, including sharing diligence under confidentiality. Specify seller consent, assignment compensation disclosures, change of control, any public/park covenants, original Optionee release and assignee assumption. No utility capacity or consultant reliance rights transfer unless separately permitted in writing. Seek transferable report reliance and application rights. No brokerage exemption, marketing authority or entitlement to compensation is assumed.

8. EXERCISE AND CLOSING. Exercise only by timely written notice under the final agreement. Proposed closing within 30 days, with a stated outside date and title objection/cure process. Complete escrow agent, deed, title standard, liens, taxes/prorations, closing costs, commissions, vacant possession and tenant rights. Optionee has no unconditional purchase obligation before valid exercise. A funded developer, not assumed founder financing, must cover the purchase balance and project obligations.

9. EXCLUSIVITY AND PROTECTION. During an enforceable paid option Seller cannot convey or encumber the property inconsistently with the granted rights. Resolve existing listing agreements and brokers. Specify confidentiality exceptions for authorized utilities, authorities, advisors and potential assignees. Any memorandum, recording, release, noncircumvention or publicity term requires negotiated language and local review.

10. TERMINATION, DEFAULT AND LOCAL TERMS. Complete notice, cure, casualty/condemnation, termination/refund rights, remedies, liability limits, venue, governing law, integration and required disclosures. No specific-performance or recordability assurance is made across states. Signature blocks and unresolved brackets must be completed by counsel after all gates pass.

ILLUSTRATIVE CASH PLAN — NOT QUOTED OR FUNDED
$500 initial + $1,000 possible extension = $1,500 control consideration. A proposed $2,500 maximum initial learning/legal envelope makes $4,000 modeled loss if both fees and the envelope are spent and nothing is recovered. Actual professional fees, studies, application deposits, upgrades and closing costs are unquoted; $4,000 is not an all-in project estimate. Decline or obtain separate funded approval for work beyond the envelope. Respect existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative soft-control caps, one paid position, company reserve and repeat-attempt funding tests. Remaining company cash is unknown. Begin with document requests and a nonbinding no-deposit terms indication; it does not secure exclusivity.
If both fees are credited, nominal land price balance is $373,500 plus costs. The buyer/sponsor must fund it. Assignment premium is UNKNOWN. Illustrative retained receipts of $25,000 less $4,000 costs = $21,000 pretax profit; zero receipts = $4,000 loss. Break-even is 16% under those assumptions, or 24% after the project policy's 1.5 error buffer (above its 20% initial-option floor). These are economic hurdles, not forecasts. They exclude founder time and unquoted costs and must be recalculated from actual terms.

ASSIGNMENT ASSESSMENT: NOT ESTIMABLE. No supported T, D, B or C probability, acceptable seller control or buyer payment commitment has been established. Planning success definition: lawful cash assignment within 12 months after acceptable control and before expiry, producing at least $10,000 pretax net profit after all project costs. The 360-day option expires earlier than a full year, so its expiry controls. This target is not a prediction.

assignmentMethod: New inference batch: all percentages withheld as NOT ESTIMABLE under the September 23 probability standard. Historical September 22 percentages are uncalibrated judgments preserved as historical records and are not current investment estimates.
historicalMethod: 52-factor founder-pilot weights from the supplied selection-factor catalog. Conservative score = Σ(weight × evidence strength × capped rating / 5). V0=0, V1=.25 (max 2/5), V2=.55 (max 3/5), V3=.85, V4=1. Base adds half unknown weight; upper adds all unknown weight. Rank by conservative score, then evidence confidence, then state atlas score. State averages and metro proximity are context, not parcel power or fiber proof.
